/look_brief.audience: the operator's board and its lenders, who know the business and check each figure against last year
/look_brief.occasion: a three-page operating review read on screens before the meeting, then projected in the board room
/look_brief.subject_world: ferries live by timetables and harbour charts; the deck borrows only the timetable's habit of one figure per cell read across a row, and leaves out waves, hulls and nautical colour as costume with no job
/look_brief.data_character: small and tidy: one five-year revenue series, four routes by two measures with a total, three headline metrics; one exhibit per page is enough

density.target: moderate: one exhibit and a short text column per page, tables of four to six rows
density.why: three pages, few figures and a projected second reading; packing more per page would only add white space between fewer things

/look_brief.look: calm and analytical: white pages, blue-black Inter, one deep teal that leads and an ochre that points, a teal rule under a sentence title

colour_meanings.color.accent1: the company's own figures and the structure that carries them: headers, the lead series, the title rule
colour_meanings.color.accent2: the one place the claim lands: the latest year, the figure the title states
colour_meanings.color.accent3: context that should recede behind the company's figures
colour_meanings.color.positive: a signed gain, only in a bridge
colour_meanings.color.negative: a signed loss, only in a bridge

/look_brief.type_ladder: the densest page is the route table, whose 9pt cells read projected and on screen; footnotes and axis labels sit a step under at 8pt, above the 7pt floor; body at 11pt, headings at 14pt and a 22pt title that fits a claim on two lines

rejected.what: a navy and white maritime palette
rejected.why: it reads as costume and gives navy no meaning beyond ships

rejected.what: big numbers for the three headline metrics
rejected.why: alone they lose the year each is compared with, which the board reads first
labelled marks carry the values, so the grid would only add lines

/reference/page.why: a 16:9 deck read on screens and projected in a board room

/typography/roles/type.title.why: a sentence title that states the page's claim, bold and dark so it reads first

/typography/roles/type.kicker.why: a short section label above the title in the teal accent

/typography/roles/type.h1.why: a panel heading, one step under the title, in the accent

/typography/roles/type.h2.why: a bold run-in heading at body size

/typography/roles/type.body.why: body copy that reads at arm's length on a projected page

/typography/roles/type.emphasis.why: the bold run inside a body sentence

/typography/roles/type.caption.why: labels beside an exhibit, quieter than body

/typography/roles/type.footnote.why: notes at the foot, above the 7pt floor

/typography/roles/type.source_line.why: the source under each exhibit, set like a footnote

/typography/roles/type.table_header.why: bold header labels on the teal header fill

/typography/roles/type.table_cell.why: dense table rows that still read at 9pt

/typography/roles/type.axis_label.why: axis labels quieter than the data

/typography/roles/type.data_label.why: values on the marks, bold so the figure is read before the bar

/color/roles/color.surface.why: white pages that print and project cleanly

/color/roles/color.surface_alt.why: a cool pale panel and banding fill

/color/roles/color.ink.why: a blue-black text colour, softer than pure black

/color/roles/color.ink_muted.why: secondary text that still reads above 4.5:1 on white

/color/roles/color.accent1.why: the deep teal of the look: headers, the lead series, the rule

/color/roles/color.accent2.why: a warm ochre for the second series and for contrast with the teal

/color/roles/color.accent3.why: a sage for context series that should recede

/color/roles/color.rule.why: hairline rules between rows and under headers

/color/roles/color.positive.why: a green for gains in a bridge

/color/roles/color.negative.why: a red for losses in a bridge

/color/roles/color.emphasis.why: the look-here colour of a ring or box is the ochre accent

/extra_roles/color.ink_inverse.why: text on the teal header fill

/chrome.why: a teal rule under the title band ties the pages together
a quiet page number at the foot, right

/tables.why: a teal header, light banding and hairline rows: dense but calm

/charts.why: labelled marks instead of gridlines; the lead series in teal

/description.summary: A calm analytical look: white pages, blue-black Inter, a deep teal accent with an ochre second, a teal rule under a sentence title.
/description.typography: Inter throughout on a 22, 14, 11, 9, 8pt ladder; bold for titles, headings and values.
/description.color: Teal leads, ochre contrasts, sage recedes; reds and greens only for signed values.
/description.layout: 0.6in side margins, a title band above a rule, content in one or two columns on a 0.3in gutter.
/description.tables: Teal header, white bold header text, light banding, hairline rows.
/description.motifs: the teal rule under the title

/continuation.why: a page that splits repeats its title with (continued) after it
